text:
alex: quick share — ran a short bring-up pass comparing Llama-2-13b, Mistral-7b, and Qwen-7b across A100/us-west1 and H100/eu-west1. charts: https://internal.redwood/bench/179345 — high-level: H100 shows 20-35% lower p99 for long-context runs, but weird regression on Qwen when rope enabled. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: nice. can you paste the exact commands + kernel flags you used?

alex: sure — run loop for single replica, warm cache, measured 32k context with kv-cache enabled. command: ```./bench_tool --model qwen-7b --quant nf4 --rope on --kernel auto --ctx 32768 --batch 1 --gpu a100``` then same with `--gpu h100`.

ingrid: when you say "rope on" what implementation? classic RoPE vs phase-shift? that matters for Qwen.

alex: `rope=phase_shift` (we used the new phase-shift fallback). metrics: A100: p99=2450ms, tokens/s ~82; H100: p99=1560ms, tokens/s ~112. but with Mistral we get p99 A100=1300ms vs H100=980ms. Llama is closer to Mistral on A100. Qwen however on H100 exhibits spikes ~4s occasionally when sequence crosses 16k boundary.

sam: can you dump kernel selection logs? the runtime should pick `flash_attn_v3` for H100 and maybe `flash_attn_v2` for A100 depending on seq len.

alex: pasted kernel log snippet: ```[kernel_choice] model=qwen-7b seq=32768 selected=rope_phase_shift_fast fallback=rope_generic kernels=(flash_attn_v3,flash_attn_v2)```

juan: hmm if selected=rope_phase_shift_fast then fallback shouldn't be happening. do you see fallthroughs in the trace?

alex: yes in ~7% of requests we see fallthrough to `rope_generic` with a note "unsupported block size -> fallback". appears only on H100.

maya: could be a kernel codegen mismatch for warp sizes on H100 SMs. @infra-bot did we push the H100 kernel patch last week?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-runtime v3.14 deployed to eu-west1-h100 pool at 2026-03-05T02:12:00Z.

ingrid: if kernel v3.14 shipped, maybe phase-shift fast path has an edge-case with sequence mod 512. try `--rope=phase_shift_strict` or set `--seq-pad=512` as a quick test. Also try `--batch 2` to see if batching avoids the edge.

alex: reran with `--seq-pad=512` on H100: fallthroughs dropped to 0. p99 stabilized to 1480ms, throughput +6%. good catch.

sam: sounds like kernel expects aligned blocks. we should add an auto-pad option in the runtime when `rope_phase_shift_fast` selected. file a small PR?

juan: also capture accuracy/regression evals — pad could slightly shift position embeddings for edge cases. run eval set for GQA and long-context tasks.

alex: agreed — running a small eval now (200 prompts) to compare logits diff with and without pad. quick numbers: mean KL=3.2e-5, exact-match delta negligible so far.

maya: next steps: 1) infra: mark kernel as requiring auto-pad in H100 until codegen fix, 2) eng-ml: add runtime flag `rope_auto_pad` default true for phase-shift fast path, 3) bench: schedule full throughput matrix for 8k/32k/64k across A100/H100 next week.

juan: +1. create a canary job in eu-west1 that runs the pad-enabled runtime on 10% traffic for Qwen-7b long-context routes.

alex: creating ticket and canary now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
